text:
Mira: quick mock attached — moved the variant toggle from the right edge into the row, so it sits before the traffic slider. link: https://files.redwood/mock/variant-toggle-v2.png
Mira: main concern = keyboard order & screen reader reading order. visually it feels more discoverable but might confuse SR users who expect controls after the name.
Lee: agree re: SR. If toggle is before the name we need to ensure the accessible name reads like "Variant A — toggle on/off" so it flows. Otherwise NVDA/JAWS will announce toggle then name which is odd.
Lee: recommendation: keep DOM order = visually-left-to-right order, and add aria-labelledby referencing the variant label, e.g. <button aria-labelledby="variant-a-label variant-a-toggle">
Jae: small frontend note: if we keep it in the row we must ensure the focus target is >=44px and focus ring is visible. current CSS clip-path for compact rows will chop focus.
Jae: proposed markup snippet:
```html
<label id="variant-a-label">Variant A</label>
<button id="variant-a-toggle" aria-pressed="false">Enable</button>
```
Jae: also add visually-hidden text for screen readers when we show percent allocations ("10% traffic to Variant A") so SR users get the context.
Toni: copy q: should toggle label be "Enable variant" or "Start canary for Variant A"? Product thinking: explicit action is better "Start canary — Variant A" since toggles trigger runtime rollouts.
Mira: +1 explicit copy. If people accidentally toggle we need clearer affordance and an undo.
Sam: backend / telemetry: if toggle triggers a rollout we need to emit event: rollout_manual_start with metadata {variant, user, method: "ui_toggle"}. keyboard toggles vs mouse should be the same event.
Sam: also consider gating: if the config requires multi-step (review checklist) the toggle should open a confirmation drawer rather than immediate flip.
Lee: accessibility for confirmations: when confirmation opens, set focus to the modal header and add aria-modal. For toasts we should use aria-live="polite" so screen readers notice the rollout started.
Mira: about undo placement — do we want inline "Undo" next to the toggle or a toast with Undo action? Inline might clutter rows but is discoverable.
Jae: technical tradeoff: inline undo requires us to reserve space and update layout when toast appears. toast is simpler and consistent with other actions (deploy, revert).
Sam: ops opinion: toast + timeline entry. Keep undo in toast for 10s, and also create a timeline event row with a reversible action (rollback) in history. That way we don't need inline chrome.
Toni: that sounds good. UX question: when toast is open and user tabs, where should focus land? Back to the toggle or onto the toast?
Lee: best practice = focus stays on the control that triggered the action (toggle). Toast should be reachable via a live region link "View rollout details" with proper skip link pattern.
Mira: contrast: moving toggle to the left means toggle color and label are near variant name. we need 4.5:1 contrast for label text against background. Sam can we get a quick color pass?
Sam: I'll run the palette through contrast checker and push a token update if needed.
Jae: i'll mock the keyboard flow and add a keyboard-only video clip to the Figma file.
deploy-bot: snapshot uploaded: designs/variant-toggle-v2/keyboard-flow.mp4
Toni: action items:
- Mira: update mock to include explicit "Start canary — Variant A" copy and show toast mock (due EOD)
- Jae: add accessible markup + keyboard video to Figma (tomorrow)
- Lee: write a short A11y checklist we can attach to the PR (48h)
- Sam: run color contrast and confirm telemetry event name (rollout_manual_start) (ASAP)
Mira: any objections to toast + timeline rollback pattern?
Lee: no objections. :thumbsup:
Jae: fine by me, will prototype focus management.
Toni: great — let's review on Fri sync.
Mira: thanks everyone, moving mock into updated frame now. :sparkles:
